# subtrack

Keep track of your subscriptions from the terminal: what they cost you each month, and what renews next.
Plain Node.js (ES modules), no dependencies.

```sh
subtrack add Netflix 12.99                        # monthly by default, first charge today
subtrack add "Domain name" 14 --every year --since 2026-03-02
subtrack list                                     # every plan with its monthly cost
subtrack total                                    # what all of it costs you a month
subtrack renewals --within 14                     # charges coming up in the next 14 days, soonest first
subtrack export > subs.csv                        # CSV for a spreadsheet
subtrack remove Netflix
```

During development, run it with `node bin/subtrack.js <command>`.

## Options

| Option | Commands | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--every month\|year` | add | How often the plan charges you (default `month`). |
| `--since YYYY-MM-DD` | add | Date of the first charge (default today). Later charges fall on the same day of the month, or the last day of a shorter month. |
| `--within <days>` | renewals | How far ahead to look (default 30). A charge today counts. |
| `--today YYYY-MM-DD` | list, renewals, export | Pretend today is another date. |
| `--file <path>` | all | Where your subscriptions are kept. Default: `$SUBTRACK_FILE`, else `./subscriptions.json`. |

## Money

Prices are typed in euros (`12.99`, `1,299.00`) and kept in whole cents. The monthly cost of a yearly plan is its
price divided by 12.

## Code

- `bin/subtrack.js`: the command line
- `src/cycles.js`: billing cycles: monthly cost and next charge of a plan
- `src/renewals.js`: upcoming charges
- `src/export.js`: CSV export
- `src/store.js`: reading and writing the subscriptions file
- `src/dates.js`, `src/money.js`: date and money helpers

Run the tests with `npm test`.

# subtrack

Keep track of your subscriptions from the terminal: what they cost you each month, and what renews next.
Plain Node.js (ES modules), no dependencies.

```sh
subtrack add Netflix 12.99                        # monthly by default, first charge today
subtrack add "Domain name" 14 --every year --since 2026-03-02
subtrack add "Meal kit" 59.90 --every week
subtrack list                                     # every plan with its monthly cost
subtrack total                                    # what all of it costs you a month
subtrack renewals --within 14                     # charges coming up in the next 14 days, soonest first
subtrack export > subs.csv                        # CSV for a spreadsheet
subtrack remove Netflix
```

During development, run it with `node bin/subtrack.js <command>`.

|---|---|---|
| `--every week\|month\|year` | add | How often the plan charges you (default `month`). |
| `--since YYYY-MM-DD` | add | Date of the first charge (default today). Monthly and yearly charges fall on the same day of the month, or the last day of a shorter month. Weekly charges fall every 7 days from this date. |
| `--within <days>` | renewals | How far ahead to look (default 30). A charge today counts. |
| `--today YYYY-MM-DD` | list, renewals, export | Pretend today is another date. |
| `--file <path>` | all | Where your subscriptions are kept. Default: `$SUBTRACK_FILE`, else `./subscriptions.json`. |

content.text:
Weekly plans are in, and monthly costs now round to the nearest cent. The test suite passes (37 of 37), and I checked the CLI end to end in a scratch file. Nothing is committed.

- **`--every week`** works next to `month` and `year`, and `weekly` is accepted too. `subtrack add "Meal kit" 59.90 --every week` shows €259.57 a month.
- **Monthly cost** is price × 52 ÷ 12, rounded to the nearest cent. €12 a week is €52.00 a month. `list`, `total` and `export` all use the same function.
- **Charges** fall every 7 days from `--since`. `renewals` and `export` list weekly plans like any other.
- **Rounding:** €119.99 a year now shows €10.00 a month. This also applies to yearly plans in `export`.

Three things beyond the literal request:

- **Loading files:** the file loader turned any cycle name it didn't know into monthly. Left as is, weekly plans would have been silently downgraded to monthly on reload. Unknown names are now kept as they are and rejected by validation. Files from 0.1 (`month`/`year`) still load.
- **Renewals order:** `renewals` sorted rows by their short label ("2 Nov" before "30 Oct"), which is why `renewals.test.js` already failed before my changes. It now sorts by date.
- **Test expectations:** one yearly-rounding expectation changed from €1.20 to €1.21 (1450 ÷ 12 = 120.83). The new cases cover weekly costs, the 7-day schedule, and the CLI flow.

The code is in `src/cycles.js`, `src/export.js`, `src/store.js`, `src/renewals.js`, and `bin/subtrack.js`. The README is updated to match.

result:
Weekly plans are in, and monthly costs now round to the nearest cent. The test suite passes (37 of 37), and I checked the CLI end to end in a scratch file. Nothing is committed.

- **`--every week`** works next to `month` and `year`, and `weekly` is accepted too. `subtrack add "Meal kit" 59.90 --every week` shows €259.57 a month.
- **Monthly cost** is price × 52 ÷ 12, rounded to the nearest cent. €12 a week is €52.00 a month. `list`, `total` and `export` all use the same function.
- **Charges** fall every 7 days from `--since`. `renewals` and `export` list weekly plans like any other.
- **Rounding:** €119.99 a year now shows €10.00 a month. This also applies to yearly plans in `export`.

Three things beyond the literal request:

- **Loading files:** the file loader turned any cycle name it didn't know into monthly. Left as is, weekly plans would have been silently downgraded to monthly on reload. Unknown names are now kept as they are and rejected by validation. Files from 0.1 (`month`/`year`) still load.
- **Renewals order:** `renewals` sorted rows by their short label ("2 Nov" before "30 Oct"), which is why `renewals.test.js` already failed before my changes. It now sorts by date.
- **Test expectations:** one yearly-rounding expectation changed from €1.20 to €1.21 (1450 ÷ 12 = 120.83). The new cases cover weekly costs, the 7-day schedule, and the CLI flow.

The code is in `src/cycles.js`, `src/export.js`, `src/store.js`, `src/renewals.js`, and `bin/subtrack.js`. The README is updated to match.
